notes: Decode C1, C8, C16, and C24 use the prior seq32/graph128 formal campaign; Decode C32, C48, and C64 use the repeated seq64/graph256 campaign.
The Decode deployment boundary lies between C24 and C32. The connecting line is visual continuity across qualified operating points, not scaling under one unchanged deployment.
Prefill C1-C64 uses the prior seq32/graph128 formal campaign. No seq64 Prefill result is implied.
Every displayed operating point has three repetitions; the report contains 42 selected profile/concurrency runs and zero request errors.
The seq64 Decode campaign was an explicitly approved final direct-backend exception and has no HAProxy application-traffic metrics; future campaigns require HAProxy.
Host RAM readings are contaminated by approximately 196 GiB of orphaned, unmapped /dev/shm/vllm_offload_*.mmap files from prior engines and must not be interpreted as current model RAM requirements.
Process PSS/private/shared telemetry was added after these measurements and is unavailable for these historical measured windows.
seq64/graph256 KV capacity was 545216 tokens versus 568576 for seq32/graph128.
GPU energy is estimated from sampled aggregate GPU board power and excludes non-GPU system power.
PCIe RX/TX metrics are aggregate GPU endpoint rates, not direct internal PCIe-switch port counters.

reproducibility.topology: Single TP8 replica across all 8 GPUs. A profile IS an image: the entrypoint expands baked-in environment variables into the vLLM invocation (env interface: MAX_NUM_SEQS, GRAPH, MTP, MAX_BATCHED_TOKENS, MAX_MODEL_LEN, GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION, MOE_BACKEND, KV_CACHE_DTYPE, ...)

launch.profile: seq32-graph128 / seq64-graph256 (one script, profile argument selects the image)
launch.command:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the GLM-5.3 NVFP4 TP8 server for one profile.
#
# Reconstructed from the campaign's launch-and-run.sh on xe7740-04. Unlike the
# other models in this study, the configuration is not passed as flags: the
# image entrypoint expands baked-in environment variables into the vLLM
# invocation, so a profile IS an image. See deployment.yaml.
#
# The campaign produced the wide image by committing the narrow one with two
# changed variables:
#
#   docker commit --pause \
#     --change 'ENV MAX_NUM_SEQS=64' --change 'ENV GRAPH=256' \
#     radixark-glm53-graph128 local/radixark-glm53-r18-seq64-graph256:canary
#
set -euo pipefail

PROFILE="${1:?usage: launch.sh <seq32-graph128|seq64-graph256>}"
MODEL="${MODEL:-/home/demouser/models/RadixArk--GLM-5.3-NVFP4--model}"
CACHE_VOLUME="${CACHE_VOLUME:-radixark-glm53-canary-cache}"
PORT="${PORT:-8080}"

case "$PROFILE" in
  seq32-graph128)
    IMAGE=local/radixark-glm53-r18-graph128:canary
    EXPECT_SEQS=32; EXPECT_GRAPH=128 ;;
  seq64-graph256)
    IMAGE=local/radixark-glm53-r18-seq64-graph256:canary
    EXPECT_SEQS=64; EXPECT_GRAPH=256 ;;
  *) echo "unknown profile: $PROFILE" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

NAME="radixark-glm53-$PROFILE"
[[ -d $MODEL ]] || { echo "model path not found: $MODEL" >&2; exit 1; }
docker rm -f "$NAME" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

docker run -d --name "$NAME" --restart no \
  --gpus all --ipc host --security-opt label=disable \
  -p "$PORT:8080" \
  -v "$MODEL:/model:ro" \
  -v "$CACHE_VOLUME:/cache" \
  "$IMAGE"

deadline=$((SECONDS + 1800))
until curl -fsS --max-time 5 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health" >/dev/null; do
  state=$(docker inspect "$NAME" --format '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.OOMKilled}} {{.State.ExitCode}}')
  [[ $state == 'running false 0' ]] || { echo "server_failed $state" >&2; docker logs --tail 200 "$NAME" >&2; exit 1; }
  ((SECONDS < deadline)) || { echo readiness_timeout >&2; docker logs --tail 200 "$NAME" >&2; exit 1; }
  sleep 5
done

# What the engine actually configured, not what the image requested.
evidence=$(docker logs "$NAME" 2>&1 | grep -E 'non-default args:|Initializing a V1 LLM engine|GPU KV cache size' | tail -10)
printf '%s\n' "$evidence"
grep -q "max_num_seqs.: $EXPECT_SEQS" <<<"$evidence" || { echo "VERIFY max_num_seqs != $EXPECT_SEQS" >&2; exit 1; }
grep -q "max_cudagraph_capture_size.: $EXPECT_GRAPH" <<<"$evidence" || { echo "VERIFY graph != $EXPECT_GRAPH" >&2; exit 1; }
grep -q "num_spec_tokens=3" <<<"$evidence" || { echo "VERIFY num_spec_tokens != 3" >&2; exit 1; }

echo "profile_ready=$PROFILE endpoint=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT time=$(date -u --iso-8601=seconds)"

procedure.action: C32 decode throughput cliff discovered in the first formal raster
procedure.detail: Decode throughput fell off a cliff at C32 under seq32/graph128; the operating boundary was recorded rather than hidden (journal/2026-08-30-radixark-c32-throughput-cliff.md).

procedure.action: Raised active-sequence ceiling 32 to 64 and MTP3 graph capture 128 to 256
procedure.detail: Materially increased decode throughput above the cliff; one repetition per point, classified qualification evidence (journal/2026-08-31-radixark-seq64-graph256-finding.md).

procedure.action: max_num_seqs 64 to 96 with graph coverage 384; host-RAM floor measured
procedure.detail: Decode improved 19.8% above the published figure (1110.99 output tok/s, 3 repetitions, zero errors) — an unpublished improvement retained as qualification evidence. Host RAM: under a 96 GiB cgroup limit with swap disabled the container peaked at 50.33 GiB charged, zero OOM events; the 433 GiB checkpoint is streamed to VRAM by the InstantTensor loader and not retained in host RAM (journal/2026-09-06-glm53-host-ram-floor-and-parameter-raster.md).

procedure.action: Deployment contracts backfilled from ad-hoc launch scripts
procedure.detail: The runner never wrote per-run launch-command.txt/environment.txt receipts (402 run manifests, zero receipt files as of 2026-09-02), so the deployment contracts rendered on this page were reconstructed afterwards by reading the scripts that drove the campaigns. Run-to-profile mapping is inferred from directory layout and the publication selection block, not recorded as fact (DEPLOYMENTS.md).

procedure.detail: C1-C24 come from the seq32/graph128 formal campaign, C32-C64 from the repeated seq64/graph256 campaign. The connecting line is visual continuity across qualified operating points, not a scalar claim about one deployment.
